title: Maximum Walls Destroyed by Robots
summary: Given an infinite straight line with robots and walls, each robot has a bullet that can travel a certain distance.
statement: Given an infinite straight line with robots and walls, each robot has a bullet that can travel a certain distance. The bullet can be fired to the left or right, and it will destroy any walls within its range. If a bullet hits another robot, it stops at that robot and does not continue. The task is to determine the maximum number of unique walls that can be destroyed by the robots' bullets. Note that robots are immovable and are not destroyed by the bullets, and walls and robots can occupy the same position.
constraints: Up to 100,000 unique robot positions and unique wall positions.
Each robot fires once left or right within its distance; another robot blocks the shot.
Count each destroyed wall only once, including a wall at the firing robot position.
hints: After sorting robots, only adjacent robots can block a shot; overlapping destruction depends on the next robot’s direction.
Use a two-state DP from right to left and count walls in each clipped interval by binary search.
State whether the next robot fired right; try the current robot left or right with the corresponding clipping bound.
The state captures the only possible overlap boundary, and every direction assignment appears in one DP path while interval counts remain unique.
editorial: The state captures the only possible overlap boundary, and every direction assignment appears in one DP path while interval counts remain unique.
